subject: Dedicated capacity recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap and next steps

Hi Jordan 

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we have a shared action plan. Please reply with any edits/corrections.

High-level pain points you called out:
- Unpredictable tail latency on normal API endpoints during peak traffic windows (spikes tied to batch jobs).
- Data isolation / HIPAA controls required for PHI processing  need VPC-only access and customer-managed KMS.
- Cost variability during sudden traffic spikes; want predictable unit economics for planning.

Goals we agreed on:
- Dedicated GPU capacity in us-east-1 to guarantee throughput and isolation.
- 95th/99th latency targets: initial target <=200ms (95th) for standard generation; SLA discussed below.
- Ability to pin to a model version and have automated rollouts with canary testing.
- Security/compliance: SOC2-aligned logs, audit history, and support for customer KMS.

Proposed dedicated config (initial):
- Reserved pool: 4 x A100 (40GB) instances reserved 24/7 in us-east-1.
- Autoscale policy: warm pool + burst to 12 GPUs during peak (policy: scale when 80% utilization sustained for 5m).
- Network: Private VPC peering with customer-managed routes, option for private control plane.
- SLA target: 99.9% uptime for the dedicated service; we can discuss 99.95% as a paid uplift.

Security/compliance notes:
- We will provide a completed security questionnaire and sample SOC2 artifacts.
- Data at rest encrypted with customer KMS (we support AWS KMS/HSM integrations).

Next steps / owners:
1) Redwood: update proposal with exact pricing for 4 reserved + autoscale to 12; include SLA uplift options (Marissa)  deliver by EOD 5/03.
2) ACME: confirm timeline target (you mentioned a July 1 target) and any procurement constraints (Jordan).
3) Technical deep dive: schedule a 60m session with your infra/security team to walk VPC/KMS/networking (Rishi to lead).
4) Complete security questionnaire and return to us (ACME security).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf (draft pricing + config) and acme-security-questions.xlsx (we'll use your answers to finalize).

If this looks right I'll send an updated proposal that reflects the autoscale & SLA uplift options.

Thanks 
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Walker <elliot.walker@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa  this is a great summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- The latency target is correct; we'd like the 95th <=200ms and for the 99th to be <400ms if possible.
- We do require strict HIPAA controls. Encryption at rest with our KMS is required (not optional). Please mark that as a hard requirement in the proposal.
- SLA: 99.95% would be preferable; I understand that's an uplift  please include both 99.9% and 99.95% options.
- Timeline: July 1 rollout would be ideal. Procurement will need a final quote and standard PO terms by mid-June.

We'll plan to have our security team fill out the questionnaire and send it back by next week. Also, please confirm whether you support VPC peering or if only PrivateLink is supported  our networking team will need that detail for the technical deep dive.

Appreciate it  Jordan
Jordan Smith
Director of Engineering, Acme Health
jordan.smith@acmehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0998

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap and next steps

Jordan  thanks for the quick clarifications. Confirming next actions: 
- I'll produce an updated proposal (redwood-dedicated-proposal-v2.pdf) that sets encryption-at-rest to customer KMS as a required item, and that includes two SLA tiers: 99.9% (standard) and 99.95% (premium uplift).
- Networking: we support both VPC peering and PrivateLink. For HIPAA scenarios, most customers choose VPC peering + private control plane; Rishi will walk through pros/cons in the technical deep dive.
- Timeline: we'll target final proposal by EOD 5/03 and follow up to get a mid-June PO target to hit a July 1 rollout.

Rishi  can you propose two 60m slots for next week for the deep dive with Acme infra/security? Prefer mornings PST.

Ben  I'll include the premium SLA pricing; can you confirm ballpark uplift (%) for 99.95% vs 99.9% so I can call it out in the proposal?

Jordan  attaching the updated draft now. Let me know if you'd like the proposal formatted as a DocuSign-ready quote.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v2.pdf

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: ACME proposal & ask

Internal note  quick summary and asks so we can finalize pricing: 
- Customer: Acme Health (HIPAA). They require customer-managed KMS + VPC peering.
- Initial reserved config: 4 x A100 (reserved), burst/autoscale to 12 GPUs during peaks.
- SLA: they asked for 99.95% as preferred; we should provide both 99.9% and 99.95% options.
- Timeline: aiming for July 1 rollout; procurement needs final by mid-June.

Asks: 
1) Ben  please confirm the uplift percentage for 99.95% SLA and any minimum term constraints.
2) Rishi  please prepare network diagram bullets (VPC peering vs PrivateLink) and a checklist for the technical deep dive (KMS, routing, firewall rules).

I'll send the updated proposal and schedule the deep dive once I have the slots from Rishi and Ben's SLA uplift.

-Marissa
